product.sinclair-pc200.summary: The Amstrad compact that brought the Sinclair name to the British PC-compatible market.
product.sinclair-pc200.history: Amstrad sold the Sinclair PC200 in Britain in 1988 as a home PC for work and games. In November, Your Sinclair listed £299 without a monitor, £399 with a monochrome monitor and £499 with a colour monitor, plus VAT.
product.sinclair-pc200.technical.archite: A television could serve as the display. The service manual specifies an 8 MHz 8086, CGA for television or monitor, and MDA for a monitor only. The RF modulator works in CGA mode.
product.sinclair-pc200.technical.firmwar: The preserved BIOS identifies the machine as a Sinclair PC200. Two 8 KiB dumps are interleaved to form 16 KiB and the reset vector jumps to FC00:205B.
product.sinclair-pc200.technical.verifie: BluMach includes the shared pc200 profile. The hashes were verified and the BIOS was examined statically.
product.sinclair-pc200.technical.limitat: The chip revision still needs to be checked on a physical machine and booting validated in BluMach.
